solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Vehicle marking cops? (5,3)

blocks.note: the surface asks what vehicle could 'mark' a person, as in singling them out
read as a vehicle that bears police markings: the livery tells everyone the cops are in it

annotation.surface: A question about what identifies a police officer's transport.
annotation.walkthrough: There is no letter wordplay: the question mark flags that 'marking' is being stretched from singling out to wearing markings.
annotation.definitionFit: A squad car is a police patrol car, the vehicle that marks out officers on duty.

entries.clue: Parties [of] amateur mapmakers hiked up sierra (7)

indicatorNotes.hiked up: in a down clue, raising a word makes it read from the bottom up

blocks.note: laic = lay, not professional
OS = Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapmakers; with LAIC, hiked up to read upwards
Sierra is S in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: A club of hobbyist mapmakers heads up a mountain range together.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Amateur mapmakers' looks like one group of hobbyists, but it splits in two before the pair is turned upside down. The Ordnance Survey is the UK's official map agency.
annotation.definitionFit: Socials are informal parties, such as a club or church social.

entries.clue: One’s leaving most of liquid waste [in] vessel (3)

indicatorNotes.leaving: the I ('one') departs from the word
indicatorNotes.most of: all but the final letter is kept

blocks.note: urine is liquid bodily waste
one = I, which is taken out
the last letter, E, is dropped

annotation.surface: Someone walking out on a pot of sewage.
annotation.walkthrough: Two removals in a row: first the I goes, then the tail E is cut off.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an urn is a large vase or container, so a vessel in the pottery sense rather than a ship.

entries.clue: Cream dairy built [for] long-lasting quality (10)

indicatorNotes.Cream: to cream an opponent is to thrash them, so the letters get beaten into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 10 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: Advice to make cream at a sturdily built dairy that lasts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cream dairy' reads as farm produce, but 'Cream' is a verb meaning beat hard, telling you to rearrange DAIRY BUILT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: durability names the property that long-lasting things have.

entries.clue: Dressing[’s] a fiddle having lost coat (5)

indicatorNotes.having lost coat: a word's coat is its outside, so the first and last letters go

blocks.note: used as written
a fiddle is a VIOLIN; stripping its outer letters V and N leaves IOLI

annotation.surface: A violin that has been stripped of its varnish, or a swindle exposed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' could be a scam, but here it is the instrument, the VIOLIN.
annotation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise used as a dressing or dip.

entries.clue: Orbiter linked to Mars rovers on surface of planet (6)

indicatorNotes.on: in an across clue, A on B puts A after B
indicatorNotes.surface of: the surface of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter of planet
hobos are wandering tramps

annotation.surface: A satellite relaying signals from the Mars rovers on the planet's surface.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is space exploration, so 'rovers' suggests robot vehicles; here they are human wanderers, HOBOS.
annotation.definitionFit: Phobos is the larger of the two moons orbiting Mars.

entries.clue: House fire in US [could be] malicious prank (4)

blocks.note: HO is the standard abbreviation for house
to fire someone is to give them the axe, spelt AX in America

annotation.surface: A false alarm about an American house fire.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fire' is not flames but dismissal, and 'in US' asks for the American spelling AX rather than AXE.
annotation.definitionFit: A hoax is a deception played on people, often with malice.

entries.clue: Book digests just scrap source of many ideas (6,5)

indicatorNotes.digests: what is digested is taken inside

blocks.note: BK is the abbreviation for book
just = right, fair
a scrap is a fight; to spar is to fight

annotation.surface: A digest of an author's work that just throws away an inspirational source.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Book digests' pretends to be a Reader's Digest summary; it is the book abbreviation swallowing two words. 'Scrap' looks like rubbish, but it is a scuffle.
annotation.definitionFit: A bright spark is a clever, lively person full of ideas.

entries.clue: Toss back short-tailed shark (7)

indicatorNotes.short-tailed: the word's tail, its last letter, is cut off

blocks.note: to shy is to throw, as at a coconut shy
the back of a ship is the STERN; dock the N

annotation.surface: A fisherman throwing back a shark that has lost part of its tail.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is angling, but 'shark' is a crook, and 'back' is the stern of a boat, not a direction.
annotation.definitionFit: A shyster is an unscrupulous operator, especially a lawyer: a shark.

entries.clue: An old woman adopting stuck-up air of cultivation (8)

indicatorNotes.adopting: the old woman takes the next piece into her family, inside her
indicatorNotes.stuck-up: in a down clue, 'up' makes the word read bottom to top

blocks.note: an = A
a gran is a grandmother
AIR written upwards

annotation.surface: An elderly lady taking on snobbish, superior airs.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stuck-up' pretends to mean snooty; in a down clue it means written upwards, and 'adopting' has the old woman take the upturned air into her home.
annotation.definitionFit: Agrarian means relating to the cultivation of land.

entries.clue: Description of verse could be focus of Mass (6,2,7)

blocks.note: the middle letter of GRAVITY is V, the abbreviation for verse
the point where an object's mass is balanced

annotation.surface: A church service being analysed: the verse sung could be the heart of the Mass.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a church Mass, but it is mass in physics. The first definition is cryptic: V (verse) sits right in the centre of GRAVITY.
annotation.definitionFit: The centre of gravity is the point where a body's mass acts as if concentrated.

entries.clue: Land excellent jab striking face of boxer in brazen burst (10)

indicatorNotes.striking face of: striking out the front letter of BOXER, its B, from JAB
indicatorNotes.in: the pieces sit inside the rearranged word
indicatorNotes.burst: BRAZEN is broken apart and reassembled

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written AI
JAB loses B, the first letter of boxer
BRAZEN rearranged, burst open so the other two pieces fit inside

annotation.surface: A boxer landing a superb jab to the face in a bold flurry.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Land' looks like the verb to land a punch; it is the definition, a country. A1 for excellent is written AI in crosswords.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Azerbaijan is one land, a country in the Caucasus.

entries.clue: Estate managers cut cereal crops south of river (11)

indicatorNotes.south of: in a down clue, below: the river comes first

blocks.note: the Exe is a river in Devon
used as written
rice is a cereal crop

annotation.surface: Farm managers harvesting grain beside a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Estate' suggests a country farm, but it is a dead person's estate; executrices are female executors of a will.
annotation.definitionFit: Executrices are women appointed to administer a dead person's estate.

entries.clue: Spot wife in front of buffet (4)

indicatorNotes.in front of: W comes before the next piece

blocks.note: W = wife, as in genealogies
to buffet is to strike, HIT

annotation.surface: Someone spotting a wife standing ahead at the buffet table.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' is a food table in the surface and a blow in the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A whit is a tiny amount, a spot, as in 'not a whit'.

entries.clue: Corporal[’s] obsessive checking of smallest thing (10)

indicatorNotes.checking: to check is to hold back, restrain: ANAL holds the next piece inside

blocks.note: anal = obsessively fussy
atomic = relating to an atom, the smallest thing

annotation.surface: A fussy army NCO inspecting the tiniest details.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Corporal' is not the army rank but the adjective meaning bodily. AN(ATOMIC)AL.
annotation.definitionFit: A less common sense: corporal as an adjective means relating to the body, the field anatomy studies.

entries.clue: American thoroughly beat darn punching bag (7)

indicatorNotes.punching: HELL punches into the bag, ending up inside it

blocks.note: darn and hell are both mild oaths
a sac is a bag-like pouch

annotation.surface: An American boxer cursing as they pummel a punchbag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Punching bag' reads as one object but splits into an insertion instruction and the container. 'Darn' is the mild oath, not mending, and the whole shellac-as-thrash sense is American slang.
annotation.definitionFit: In American slang to shellac someone is to defeat them soundly.

entries.clue: Copper led empty investigation up close (3-2-3)

indicatorNotes.empty: LED emptied of its middle leaves L and D
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, CASE is written upwards

blocks.note: Cu is copper's chemical symbol
LED without its middle E
a case is an investigation; up, it reads ESAC

annotation.surface: A police officer running a hollow inquiry right up close.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is a copper and an investigation, so 'close' looks like proximity. It is a noun: in Britain a close is a dead-end residential street.
annotation.definitionFit: A cul-de-sac is a street closed at one end, which British addresses often call a close.

entries.clue: Turning 15, perhaps attention-seeker[’s] one to charge (7)

indicatorNotes.Turning: the pieces are turned round to read backwards

blocks.note: 15 across is SHELLAC, one kind of resin
'Oi!' is shouted to get attention

annotation.surface: A show-off turning fifteen and charging about.
annotation.walkthrough: '15' points to the answer at 15 across, SHELLAC, and 'perhaps' shows it stands for the class it is an example of. 'Turning' covers both pieces together.
annotation.definitionFit: An ioniser is a device that gives air particles an electric charge.

entries.clue: Save short presentation after area meeting at an end (7)

indicatorNotes.short: the last letter is lopped off
indicatorNotes.after: 'after' means following in time, so the later pieces come behind A

blocks.note: A = area
save = but, except
a talk is a presentation; cut short, TAL

annotation.surface: Shortening a talk that follows a regional meeting drawing to a close.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Short presentation' sounds like a brief talk, and that is literal: TALK cut short. 'Save' means except, not rescue.
annotation.definitionFit: An abuttal is where one piece of land meets another at its boundary.

entries.clue: Small cinema complex screens not all there (7)

indicatorNotes.complex: CINEMA is tangled into a new arrangement
indicatorNotes.screens: to screen is to hide, so the rearranged letters hold S inside

blocks.note: anagram of CINEMA
S = small, as on clothing labels

annotation.surface: A little multiplex showing films that are not the full versions.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cinema complex' and 'screens' belong together in the surface; in the wordplay 'complex' rearranges and 'screens' hides S: AMNE(S)IC.
annotation.definitionFit: Someone amnesic has lost part of their memory, so it is not all there.

entries.clue: Exceedingly hot flan base (3,4)

indicatorNotes.base: base means debased, corrupt: the letters are corrupted into a new order

blocks.note: anagram fodder, 7 letters
anagram indicator

annotation.surface: A remark that the bottom of a pastry case is extremely hot.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Flan base' is a pastry shell in the surface; 'base' is the anagram signal. NOT HALF is British slang meaning very much.
annotation.definitionFit: In British speech 'not half' means extremely, as in 'it was not half hot'.

entries.clue: Wood slab propped up in hearthside glow (7)

indicatorNotes.propped up: in a down clue, lifted to read from the bottom up

blocks.note: fir is a wood
a tile is a slab; written upwards

annotation.surface: A wooden slab propped by the fireplace, glowing in the firelight.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface lays out a fireside scene, and the answer belongs right in it.
annotation.definitionFit: A firelit room is lit by the glow from the hearth.

entries.clue: Performed round with King[’s] Singer (4)

indicatorNotes.round: turned round, so the word reads backwards
indicatorNotes.with: 'with' means accompanied by, so K keeps it company at the end

blocks.note: performed = ran (as a machine runs); turned round, NAR
K = king in chess

annotation.surface: A vocalist who sang a round alongside the King.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Singer' is capitalised to look like a vocalist; it is someone who sings to the police. A nark is British slang for an informer.
annotation.definitionFit: A nark is a police informer, and to sing is to inform.

entries.clue: Energy boards beat regulator [and] arbitrator (10)

indicatorNotes.boards: E boards the next word as a passenger boards a ship, getting inside

blocks.note: a pacemaker regulates the heartbeat
E = energy, boarding just behind the first letter

annotation.surface: A power company board meeting to fix an electricity regulator and appoint an adjudicator.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Beat' suggests defeating the regulator, but here it is a heartbeat, and 'boards' is the insertion verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: an arbitrator's job is settling disputes, which makes them a maker of peace.

entries.clue: Before training, call out underground cell (5)

indicatorNotes.Before: the second piece comes before training, so training goes last

blocks.note: to cry is to call out
PT = physical training

annotation.surface: A coach shouting before a training session.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is written in reverse order: 'Before training' tells you the call comes first, even though training is read first.
annotation.definitionFit: A crypt is an underground chamber, often beneath a church.

entries.clue: Shortly plan online stores (4)

indicatorNotes.stores: the phrase stores the answer inside it

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of 'plan' and the start of 'online'

annotation.surface: A brief plan for an online shop.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stores' looks like shops in an online plan; it is the verb, holding the answer inside 'plan online'.
annotation.definitionFit: Anon is an old word for soon, shortly.

entries.clue: Plastic colanders plugged by choosy cooking academy (9,6)

indicatorNotes.Plastic: plastic means mouldable, so COLANDERS is reshaped
indicatorNotes.plugged by: the first group of letters is filled by the second
indicatorNotes.cooking: CHOOSY is cooked up into a new order

blocks.note: anagram of COLANDERS
CHOOSY rearranged, filling a gap near the end of the first anagram

annotation.surface: A fussy cookery school stocked with plastic colanders.
annotation.walkthrough: Both anagrams are hiding in a kitchen scene, and 'academy' is the British word for a kind of state secondary school.
annotation.definitionFit: In Britain an academy is a type of state-funded secondary school.

entries.clue: Picked up delivery of half-dozen eggs (3)

indicatorNotes.Picked up: picked up by the ear, heard

blocks.note: in cricket an over is a set of six balls delivered by one bowler

annotation.surface: Collecting a delivery of six eggs.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface is groceries, but 'delivery' is a cricket term: a bowler's six-ball over, which in British speech sounds like OVA.
annotation.definitionFit: Ova is the plural of ovum, an egg cell.

entries.clue: Like to enter clubs wearing golf jacket (6)

indicatorNotes.to enter: AS goes into the letters that follow

blocks.note: C = clubs, the card suit
like = as
in = wearing, as in 'in a hat'
Golf is G in the NATO alphabet

annotation.surface: Wanting to walk into the golf club wearing a smart jacket.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' and 'golf' belong together in the surface but are separate letters here: AS enters C-IN-G.
annotation.definitionFit: A casing is an outer covering, a jacket, as on a pipe or boiler.

entries.clue: Firm searches packaging at counter (8)

indicatorNotes.packaging: packaging wraps a product, so the first word wraps around AT
indicatorNotes.counter: running counter means going the opposite way, so it is read backwards

blocks.note: to trawl is to search thoroughly
used as written: TRAWL(AT)S, then reversed

annotation.surface: A company going through packages at the shop counter.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business in this shop scene; it is an adjective, steadfast. 'Counter' is the reversal sign, not a shop fitting.
annotation.definitionFit: An adjective sense: firm here means steadfast and dependable, not a company, and stalwart supporters are exactly that.
